key_insight: CoCoT-EEG argues that EEG foundation models work better when they learn via contrastive pretraining at multiple scales, rather than relying mainly on masked reconstruction of raw signals. This better matches EEG’s noisy, low-dimensional, frequency-specific structure.
problem_solved: Existing self-supervised EEG foundation models often use tokenization plus masked reconstruction, which can be suboptimal for noisy signals where useful information is concentrated in narrow frequency bands and limited temporal/spatial dimensions.
method: Uses a contrastive-pretrained multiscale convolutional transformer tailored to EEG decoding.
Learns representations across multiple temporal scales to capture both fine-grained and broader EEG patterns.
Combines convolutional feature extraction with transformer-based contextual modeling for robust self-supervised pretraining.
impact: This approach can improve EEG representation learning for downstream decoding tasks, making foundation models more practical for non-invasive brain-signal analysis. For practitioners, it suggests that domain-specific pretraining objectives can outperform generic masked reconstruction strategies on challenging biosignals.

paper_title: CoCoT-EEG: Contrastive-Pretrained Multiscale Convolutional Transformer for EEG Decoding
paper_authors: Gabriel Mahuas, Victoria Shevchenko, Ugo Tanielian, Yassir Bendou, Richard Gao
